comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 formal OER: year-one rules for 2026 entrants, year-two rules for 2025 entrants, year-three rules for 2024 entrants
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 formally adopted OER specifies different active entering cohorts for each year, with 60 EC in first year, 56 EC in second and 64 EC in third: 180 EC across the documented course structure. The public year pages describe the same thematic and clinical progression. This cross-cohort reconstruction illustrates one complete published structural pathway, not a promise that the same details apply to one Fall 2026 student over all three future years. The 4.5-EC free second-year choice, 11-EC research minor and 14-EC clinical minor are preserved as choice space; no elective content is invented. Distinct semester patient-contact, practice and professional components are retained rather than buried inside broad thematic credits. There is no separately named bachelor thesis; the 7-EC year-two scientific research project is the identifiable independent-research component. The medical bachelor is part of a longer professional route and UCR courses do not confer clinical qualification.

alternatives.label: Human health, disease and behaviour
alternatives.concept: A biomedical and health-science curriculum linking human anatomy and physiology, cellular disease mechanisms, infection, pharmacology, neuroscience, psychology and evidence-based public health. It is the strongest academically feasible UCR response to medical subjects and patient-centred health questions, but it contains no supervised clinical placements, medical examination skills or pathway to physician qualification.
alternatives.labelReason: The actual programme comprises a sustained biomedical, cognitive and psychological sequence with epidemiology, laboratory and evidence-synthesis courses; the label names its health and disease content without presenting it as Medicine or clinical training.
progression: Foundations of Life, Health & Biomedicine and Introduction to Brain & Behavior precede their formally dependent specialist courses. Introductory disease, neuroscience and social psychology appear before later related 300-level work where available; all prerequisites and planned semester offerings pass.

candidates.label: Supervised clinical medicine and patient care
candidates.reason: A distinct clinically oriented second alternative would require sustained supervised patient care, physical examination and clinical diagnosis. UCR teaches relevant anatomy, disease science, health psychology and ethical reasoning but has no medical practice or patient-contact courses to form a defensible 24-course clinical pathway. These components remain substantive gaps, not cosmetic substitutions.

candidates.label: Research on disease from molecules to populations
candidates.reason: The first UCR programme already gives this direction its substantive curriculum through molecular biology, organ-level disease, neuroscience, epidemiology, laboratory methods and systematic evidence synthesis; a separate title would duplicate its main organising logic.

selection.assessment: The 24-course programme is a strong UCR academic response to disease mechanisms, public health, cognition and patient experience, with clinically specific training explicitly absent. A second medical-practice route cannot be supported by UCR patient contact, examination or clinical reasoning courses; research from molecules to populations is already a core emphasis of the first programme.

notes.text: Radboud Medicine integrates biomedical science with repeated patient contact, clinical reasoning, examination skills and professional practice as part of physician training. UCR offers a substantial academic programme in human health, disease and behaviour, but does not offer medical clinical training or a route to physician qualification.
